scores.claim_text: Teal Drones selected for SRR T2 Program of Record; awarded $1.5M prototype contract; will compete for SRR T2 production contract.
supports: usaspending pre-cutoff DoD awards to TEAL DRONES INC = $257,827 across 8 awards (2019-2023-01-15), heavily Air Force / Army purchase orders for Golden Eagle UAS — corroborates a real DoD relationship
usaspending DoD awards to Teal cumulative through 2026 = $2.16M / 27 awards — confirms continuing federal-customer presence after cutoff (NOT relied upon for scoring)

pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for 'Short Range Reconnaissance', 'Short Range Reconnaissance Tranche 2', 'SRR', 'Blue sUAS', contractor 'Teal Drones' / 'Red Cat' / 'Teal' — corpus does not cover the SRR sUAS procurement line
scores.interpretation: Rubric heuristic 7: NOT_FOUND in the 410-PE corpus is not a negative — the J-Book corpus is heavy on DARPA/MDA/SOCOM/USAF/USSF RDT&E and does not cover Army sUAS procurement lines. SRR is an Army sUAS Program of Record administered through PEO Aviation; expected to be a small P-40 procurement item that did not enter the corpus. The prototype-contract claim itself is corroborated directly by usaspending Teal awards, and the forward production-contract language is a competitive expectation, not a booked claim. Mark UNVERIFIABLE / coverage gap rather than failing the claim.

scores.claim_text: Teal's Golden Eagle was a Blue sUAS list approved drone (Aug 2020) and Teal won an SRR T1 prototype.
supports: usaspending pre-cutoff DoD awards include multiple Golden Eagle UAS purchase orders (W913E521F0005, N0018921P0215, W912HZ21PV003, W911S221P1016) across Army, Navy, and CRREL customers — consistent with Blue sUAS list authorization driving low-dollar GSA-style buys
pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for Blue sUAS / SRR T1 — corpus coverage gap (heuristic 7)
scores.interpretation: Historical-fact claim (Blue sUAS approval + SRR T1 prototype). USAspending shows real, varied Golden Eagle purchases by DoD customers consistent with Blue-list authorization. J-Book absence is a corpus gap, not a falsifier. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Teal anchors Enterprise segment and is expected to drive segment revenues in fiscal 2023; government customers expected to be the most significant FY2023 revenue drivers.
supports: pre-cutoff (2019 to 2023-01-15) total federal obligations to Teal Drones across DoD+DHS = ~$1.30M cumulative across ~9 awards (DoD $258K + DHS $1.05M one BPA call) — small in absolute terms

FY2022 total Red Cat revenue per filing = $6.43M; pre-cutoff cumulative federal obligations represent roughly 20% of one fiscal year, but spread across multiple years — current federal run-rate is meaningfully less than the 'most significant revenue driver' framing implies
pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for Teal / SRR / Blue sUAS (coverage gap, not a falsifier)
scores.M_value: pre-cutoff federal obligations ~$1.3M aggregate; ~$1.0M concentrated in single FY2022 CBP BPA call
scores.interpretation: Mode B / implied-verification: the forward narrative implies government will be the dominant revenue contributor for FY2023, but the actual trailing 12-24 month federal obligations are small relative to (i) the company's total revenue base and (ii) the magnitudes implied by the $90M CBP ceiling and SRR T2 framing. The framework cannot test future revenue, but the gap between forward language and current federal obligation run-rate is material. Flag as MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY — narrative-load-bearing concentration claim outruns the pre-cutoff data.

scores.claim_text: Teal Drones awarded a CBP multiple-award BPA with $90M ceiling over 5 years (Dec 2021).
supports: usaspending pre-cutoff DHS awards to Teal include 70B02C22F00001217 'SUAS BLUE BPA FOR USBP PMOD' $1.05M — directly corroborates the BPA exists and Teal is receiving orders against it
scores.M_value: 1 DHS award pre-cutoff totaling $1,046,806 against the BPA
scores.interpretation: Ceiling claim is accurate (it is a $90M total-ceiling, MULTIPLE-award BPA shared across 5 vendors, so Teal's effective max share is ~$18M ceiling-of-ceiling, with call orders only). Obligated-to-date as a percent of ceiling is ~1.2% (pre-cutoff), which is typical for an early-stage BPA. No falsification; PASS with note that 10-K presents ceiling but does not flag that the BPA is multi-award.

scores.claim_text: April 2022 order for 15 Golden Eagle units from a NATO Member country for deployment in Ukraine.
supports: edgar_fts fulltext search for 'Teal Drones Ukraine NATO' (cutoff 2023-01-15) returned 0 counterparty hits
scores.interpretation: Counterparty is a foreign sovereign — no SEC counterparty filing expected. Small dollar order (15 units). Cannot verify; not material enough to scrutinize. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Skypersonic awarded a five-year NASA contract for the Simulated Mars mission (Sept 2021).
supports: usaspending shows exactly ONE NASA award to SKYPERSONIC, INC.: 80NSSC21P2833, total $153,001 — 'SKYPERSONIC DRONE AND ROVER HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE TO REMOTE PILOT FOR ANALOG FIELD DEMO'
Award ID prefix '21P' and value pattern are consistent with an SBIR Phase I-style purchase order, not a five-year IDIQ
scores.M_value: 1 NASA award, $153,001 (purchase order, not multi-year IDIQ)
scores.interpretation: Mode B implied-verification: the filing describes a 'five-year contract with NASA' which connotes a sustained IDIQ. USAspending shows a single sub-$200K purchase order with no follow-on. The claim language materially overstates the program's scope and durability — classic 'press-release-grade contract' inflated into a structural narrative element. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY.

scores.claim_text: Teal operates a 13,000+ sqft Salt Lake City manufacturing facility, doubled in size January 2022.
supports: epa_frs.query_facilities for 'Teal Drones' in UT returned 0 facilities, but EPA FRS only catches facilities with environmental-reporting obligations; small drone assembly typically does not trigger FRS registration
scores.interpretation: Facility claim is operational, low-stakes, and outside the FRS coverage envelope. UNVERIFIABLE / coverage gap. No reason to suspect inflation.

scores.claim_text: Red Cat executed four acquisitions (Fat Shark, Rotor Riot, Skypersonic, Teal) in <2 years for ~$23M total, funded by ~$76M of common stock raises in 2021.
supports: acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence returned medium_coherence (0.5) on all four subsidiaries — Fat Shark (FPV goggles), Rotor Riot (e-commerce), Skypersonic (inspection software), Teal (defense sUAS) span four different end-markets

Fat Shark + Rotor Riot are consumer FPV / hobbyist (commodity hardware, falling Fat Shark revenue 9% YoY per filing); Teal + Skypersonic are defense/industrial — the consumer and defense subs share little technology or customer base

Equity raises in 2021 ($16M May + $60M July) total $76M, ~3.3x cumulative acquisition cost — consistent with raise-driven roll-up financing rather than reinvested cash flow (company has never been profitable)
scores.interpretation: Mode B implied-verification: rollup of consumer FPV gear, drone e-commerce, drone inspection software, and defense sUAS does not present a coherent operating thesis. Filing itself discloses that Fat Shark's flagship product is 'at the end of its sales cycle' (-9% YoY) while management leans the forward thesis on Teal/government — i.e., the rollup is already pivoting to a single sub-anchor. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY (incoherent acquisitions force a forward narrative dependent on one of the four subs).

summary.pentagon_jbook_note: All J-Book queries returned NOT_FOUND because the 410-PE corpus is weighted to DARPA/MDA/SOCOM/USAF RDT&E and does not cover Army small-UAS procurement lines (SRR, Blue sUAS). Per rubric heuristic 7, NOT_FOUND is treated as a corpus coverage gap, not a falsifier.
